_meta.indication: RADICAVA is indicated for the treatment of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study with a 6-month active treatment period; 123 patients randomized 1:1 to edaravone or placebo in the double-blind portion.
pivotal_trials.population: ALS patients categorized as Definite or Probable ALS by El Escorial revised Airlie House criteria, Japan ALS severity Grade 1 or 2, with onset within 2 years (Definite or Probable/EESP/2y population).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from Baseline (in Cycle 1) to the end of Cycle 6 (24 weeks) in the Revised ALS Functional Rating Scale (ALSFRS-R) score.
pivotal_trials.n: 137 patients in the double-blind phase safety analysis set (placebo n=68, edaravone n=69); 123 patients in the active phase (P-E n=58, E-E n=65).
pivotal_trials.result: Least-squares mean difference in ALSFRS-R change (edaravone – placebo) of 2.49 ± 0.76 (95% CI 0.99 to 3.98), P = 0.0013.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥10% and greater than placebo) were contusion (15% vs 9%), gait disturbance (13% vs 9%), and headache (10% vs 6%). Serious concerns include hypersensitivity/anaphylactic reactions and sulfite allergic reactions (sodium bisulfite content).
target_moa: Mechanism of action in ALS is unknown; edaravone is thought to be a free radical scavenger proposed to counter oxidative damage hypothesized to occur in the nervous system of ALS patients.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was convened; it was not deemed necessary to judge whether the data were adequate to establish efficacy or safety.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan designation granted 5/12/2015 for the treatment of ALS.

summary.text: Edaravone received orphan drug designation for ALS (5/12/2015) and was reviewed under a Standard review NDA received 6/16/16; it was approved for the treatment of ALS based on the single positive Phase 3 Study 19 with confirmatory evidence from Phase 2 Study 16. No accelerated approval, breakthrough, or priority review designations applied.

requirement.text: 3208-5: A randomized, double-blind, controlled trial of edaravone in ALS patients (Definite or Probable), randomized 1:1:1 to the approved 60 mg regimen, 60 mg with a daily/near-daily regimen, or 120 mg with a daily/near-daily regimen; primary endpoint change in ALSFRS-R over a study duration of at least 24 weeks.

citations.quote: 3208-5 Conduct a randomized, double-blind, controlled trial of edaravone in patients with ALS (definite or probable, according to ALS El Escorial Revised Airlie House criteria). Patients should be randomized (1:1:1) to the approved dosing regimen and dosage of edaravone (60 mg), the approved dosage of edaravone (60mg) with a daily or near-daily dosing regimen, or to a dosage of 120 mg of edaravone (a dosage even higher would be desirable if supported by safety data), with a daily or near-daily dosing regimen.
The primary efficacy endpoint will be the change in the revised ALS functional rating scale score (ALSFRS-R) from baseline to the end of the study. The study duration will be at least 24 weeks.
